reviews.notes: Accurately renders Krishna declaring the deepest secret wisdom combined with realization to the uncavilling Arjuna.
Faithfully renders Rājavidyā and Rājaguhyam ('A royal lore! a Kingly mystery!'), supreme sanctifier, plain to see, and inexhaustible.
Directly matches those lacking faith in this dharma returning to the cycle of mortal death without reaching the Lord.
Accurately conveys the cosmic panentheism: all beings contained in the unmanifest Lord, yet He is not contained in them.
Captures the divine paradox of yoga aiśvara: beings do not abide in Him as separate entities, while His Self sustains all.
Preserves the classic simile of the all-moving air abiding in boundless space, illustrating how all beings rest in Krishna.
Accurately represents beings entering Prakriti at kalpa's end and being projected forth anew at kalpa's beginning.
Matches projecting forth the multitude of beings again and again, helpless under the sway of material nature.
Faithfully renders Krishna sitting unattached and unenslaved by cosmic acts of creation (udāsīnavadāsīnam).
Directly renders Prakriti bringing forth moving and unmoving under the divine overseer (mayādhyakṣeṇa prakṛtiḥ).
Accurately captures foolish minds disregarding the Lord clad in human guise, unaware of His supreme sovereignty.
Directly corresponds to futile hopes, futile deeds, futile knowledge, and adopting demoniacal and deceitful natures.
Accurately matches Mahātmas grounded in the divine nature adoring with undivided minds, knowing Him as the eternal Source.
Faithfully renders satataṃ kīrtayanto mām, striving with steadfast vows and bowing down in constant devotion.
Renders the sacrifice of wisdom (jñānayajña), conceiving the Divine as Unity, diversity, and omnipresent power.
Accurately identifies Kratu, Yajna, Svadha (funeral cake), Aushadha, Mantra, Ajya (ghee), Agni, and Hutam.
Directly matches Father, Mother, Ancestor, the purifier, sacred OM, and the threefold Vedas (Rig, Sama, Yajur).
Faithfully renders the divine titles: Way (gati), Fosterer (bhartā), Lord, Witness, Abode, Refuge, Friend, and imperishable Seed.
Matches giving heat, sending and withholding rain, immortality and death, and being (sat) and non-being (asat).
Accurately presents knowers of the three Vedas drinking Soma, seeking Swarga, and enjoying divine celestial feasts in Indra's realm.
Accurately renders returning to the mortal sphere when merit is exhausted, experiencing the transitory round of coming and going.
Faithfully reflects the celebrated promise to those meditating solely on the Lord (yogakṣemaṃ vahāmyaham).
Directly matches that worship of other deities in faith is truly worship of Krishna, albeit informal/improper (avidhipūrvakam).
Captures the Lord as the enjoyer and master of all sacrifice, and how ignorance of His true nature causes men to fall back.
Accurately represents the destinations of votaries: to devas, pitris, bhūtas, and to Krishna Himself.
Faithfully renders the acceptance of humble offerings (leaf, flower, fruit, or water) made with devotion and pure intent.
Directly translates the instruction to dedicate all actions, eating, sacrifices, gifts, and austerities to the Lord.
Accurately renders liberation from karmic bondage through the yoga of renunciation and attaining union with the Lord.
Faithfully conveys the divine impartiality (samo'haṃ sarvabhūteṣu) alongside the reciprocal dwelling of devotees in God and God in them.
Matches regarding even a confirmed sinner as righteous when he turns to undivided devotion (sādhureva sa mantavyaḥ).
Faithfully presents the swift transformation into righteousness and the enduring declaration: 'none can perish, trusting Me' (na me bhaktaḥ praṇaśyati).
Accurately renders that taking refuge in Krishna allows women, Vaisyas, and Sudras alike to reach the supreme destination.
Captures the exhortation to holy Brahmins and royal sages to worship the Lord in this fleeting, unhappy world.
Accurately renders the climactic verse to fix mind and devotion on Krishna, surrender and prostrate, arriving at His peace.

chapterFindings: Chapter 9 contains a complete 1-to-1 verse translation for all 34 canonical verses without omissions or multi-verse consolidations.
The poetic transitions across metrical shifts (such as the rhymed stanzas in verses 9.20 and 9.21) maintain strict semantic alignment with the underlying Sanskrit text.
